intro.title: Write a throttle utility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a throttle utility function in JavaScript. A throttle function limits how often a given function can be executed over time, which is useful for optimizing performance in scenarios like handling rapid user input or scroll events. You will learn the core programming concept of controlling function execution timing using timers and closures. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, the setTimeout API, and managing state within a closure. By the end, you'll have a reusable throttle utility that can help make your applications more efficient.
intro.usecase: Throttling is essential for optimizing performance in interactive web applications where frequent events can overwhelm systems. In dashboard interfaces with real-time data visualizations, throttling prevents excessive API calls when users rapidly adjust date range sliders or filter controls. Search input fields use throttling to delay search execution until users pause typing, reducing unnecessary network requests. Similarly, infinite scroll implementations throttle scroll events to load content batches efficiently without janky scrolling experiences.
